code: library(fastconley) set.seed(42)  n <- 1500 d <- data.frame(lat = runif(n, 40, 46), lon = runif(n, 5, 11))  # Smooth spatial fields via an exponential-covariance Gaussian process. rad <- pi / 180 D <- 6371 * acos(pmin(1,   sin(d$lat * rad) %o% sin(d$lat * rad) +   (cos(d$lat * rad) %o% cos(d$lat * rad)) * cos(outer(d$lon, d$lon, "-") * rad))) L <- chol(exp(-D / 150) + diag(1e-8, n)) d$x <- drop(crossprod(L, rnorm(n))) + 0.5 * rnorm(n) e   <- drop(crossprod(L, rnorm(n))) + 0.5 * rnorm(n) d$y <- 1 + 0.5 * d$x + e library(fixest) est <- feols(y ~ x, data = d, demeaned = TRUE)  vcov_conley <- function(x) {   vcovSpHAC(x, lat = "lat", lon = "lon", dist_cutoff = 150,             kernel = "bartlett", dist_fn = "spherical",             ncores = 2, data = d) }  se_tab <- data.frame(   `standard errors` = c("IID", "Heteroskedasticity-robust", "Conley (150 km)"),   `se(x)` = sapply(list(vcov(est, vcov = "iid"),                         vcov(est, vcov = "hetero"),                         vcov_conley(est)),                    function(V) sqrt(diag(V))["x"]),   check.names = FALSE ) knitr::kable(se_tab, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)

code: if (requireNamespace("lfe", quietly = TRUE)) {   ## Cross-section on a regular 0.5-degree raster with holes. method =   ## "grid" forces the exact grid engine; the default method = "auto"   ## picks it automatically when the raster is large enough to win   ## (on a toy example this small, pairwise is just as fast).   set.seed(1)   cells <- expand.grid(lat = seq(40, 49.5, by = 0.5),                        lon = seq(-10, 9.5, by = 0.5))   cells <- cells[sample(nrow(cells), 600), ]   # irregular occupancy   cells$x <- rnorm(nrow(cells))   cells$y <- 0.5 * cells$x + rnorm(nrow(cells))    fit <- lfe::felm(y ~ x, data = cells, keepCX = TRUE)   V <- vcovSpHAC(fit, lat = "lat", lon = "lon",                  kernel = "bartlett", dist_fn = "spherical",                  dist_cutoff = 200, ncores = 2, method = "grid",                  data = cells)   sqrt(diag(V))    ## Panel with spatial + serial HAC (scattered points: pairwise engine)   pnl <- data.frame(unit = rep(1:200, each = 5),                     time = rep(1:5, times = 200),                     lat = rep(runif(200, 40, 50), each = 5),                     lon = rep(runif(200, -10, 10), each = 5))   pnl$x <- rnorm(nrow(pnl))   pnl$y <- 0.5 * pnl$x + rnorm(nrow(pnl))   fit2 <- lfe::felm(y ~ x | unit + time, data = pnl, keepCX = TRUE)   V2 <- vcovSpHAC(fit2, unit = "unit", time = "time",                   lat = "lat", lon = "lon", kernel = "bartlett",                   dist_fn = "haversine", dist_cutoff = 300,                   lag_cutoff = 2, balanced_pnl = TRUE, ncores = 2,                   data = pnl)   sqrt(diag(V2)) } #>          x  #> 0.03549569

code: if (requireNamespace("fixest", quietly = TRUE)) {   ## feols must be fit with demeaned = TRUE (the keepCX analogue).   set.seed(1)   cells <- expand.grid(lat = seq(40, 49.5, by = 0.5),                        lon = seq(-10, 9.5, by = 0.5))   cells$x <- rnorm(nrow(cells))   cells$y <- 0.5 * cells$x + rnorm(nrow(cells))    fit <- fixest::feols(y ~ x, data = cells, demeaned = TRUE)   vcov_fc <- function(x) {     vcovSpHAC(x, lat = "lat", lon = "lon",               kernel = "uniform", dist_fn = "spherical",               dist_cutoff = 200, ncores = 2, data = cells)   }   V <- vcov_fc(fit)   sqrt(diag(V))    ## The same wrapper can be used directly in fixest's vcov argument.   fit_sum <- summary(fit, vcov = vcov_fc)   sqrt(diag(fit_sum$cov.scaled))    ## Poisson (fepois / feglm): no demeaned = TRUE needed — the stored   ## ML scores and inverse Hessian are used directly.   cells$cnt <- rpois(nrow(cells), exp(0.4 * cells$x))   fit_pois <- fixest::fepois(cnt ~ x, data = cells)   V_pois <- vcovSpHAC(fit_pois, lat = "lat", lon = "lon",                       kernel = "uniform", dist_fn = "spherical",                       dist_cutoff = 200, ncores = 2, data = cells)   sqrt(diag(V_pois)) } #> (Intercept)           x  #>  0.03802984  0.03316774

FastGridMeat computes via FFT (arma::fft): per ring pair, even-symmetric weight vector’s (real) spectrum multiplies cached per-ring score spectra, one inverse FFT per target ring. Score spectra cached sliding latitude band plus cutoff halo, reduction deterministically chunked — results remain bit-identical across ncores. Weights use per-distance arithmetic pairwise engine (atan2 haversine, acos spherical, sqrt chord), -cell distance hard-set 0, agreement pairwise engine ~1e-15 (haversine) ~1e-12 (spherical/chord — inherent conditioning acos/sqrt near zero distance, algorithm error). "auto" rule uses FFT-aware cost model bartlett. C1-study config (2.25M cells ~1.1 km, 250 km cutoff, ~1.8e11 pairs, bartlett/spherical): 2.9 s vs 710 s 16-core pairwise engine (242x); single-threaded (20.5 s) still beats 16-core pairwise 35x. kernel’s evenness halves work (T(r2,r1) = T(r1,r2)’, upper-triangle ring pairs computed, self-ring weights halved half-meat symmetrized).

what: Dateline wrap (bug fix for global rasters)
title: fastconley 0.8.0
text: v0.7.0’s grid engine clamped longitude windows lattice edges, raster spanning full 360° circle silently missed pairs close “short way” across dateline (observed ~5e-3 relative error global test raster). engine now detects accept window reaches across dateline gap switches kernels circular windows (modular prefix-sum arcs uniform; circular convolution period n_col_full bartlett) — exact, validated pairwise engine. wrap needed lon step tile 360° evenly (consistent circular lattice exists), method = "grid" stops informative error method = "auto" falls back pairwise engine. Non-wrapping rasters unaffected: results bitwise identical v0.7.0 (verified 30-config battery).

title: fastconley 0.7.0
text: uniform kernel regular lat/lon lattice (raster cell centers, gridded covariates), within-cutoff accept set two latitude rings longitude-index interval, spatial meat reduces sliding-window sums per-ring prefix sums — FastGridMeat. Cost O(n_ring * window * n_col * k), independent pair count, accept threshold dot-product constant pairwise engine uses, result exact (agrees FP summation order; approximation anywhere natively gridded data). C1-study config (2.25M cells ~1.1 km, 250 km cutoff, ~1.8e11 pairs): 0.81 s vs 244 s 16-core pairwise engine — 302x, error 5e-15. 9M-cell continental raster (3000 x 3000, 250 km, ~7e11 pairs): 3.5 s. Supports three dist_fns (monotone chord), multiple time blocks (panels apply per period), sparse occupancy, duplicate cells, deterministic across ncores. method = "auto" (new default) switches grid engine lattice detected, kernel uniform, flop-balance estimate says wins; otherwise pairwise engine runs . Scattered (non-lattice) data unaffected. method = "grid" errors informatively requirements met. bartlett ring-FFT variant (exact per C1 study) planned follow-; bartlett rasters currently stay pairwise engine.

title: fastconley 0.6.1
text: Minor-backlog items M1-M4 notes/OPTIMIZATION_PLAN.md. Serial HAC now O(T * k) per unit instead O(T^2 * k): Bartlett--time weight decomposes sliding two-pointer window (per-block time shift conditioning). 100k-row panel T = 2000 lag = 50 computes ~6 ms. Rows must time-sorted within unit blocks (R layer always sorts; direct callers get clear error). vcovSpHAC.felm gains data =: passed frame row count fit (NAs dropped, subset), coordinates taken direct column access model-frame re-evaluation; otherwise frame overrides call-recovered data aligned model-frame path. Prep path parallelized (grid sort via TBB parallel_sort, coordinate cache trig, permutation gathers) — order-preserving, results stay bit-identical across ncores. 1M-row global cross-section 16 threads: 0.46 -> 0.21 s (scaling 2.2x -> 4.8x). Spatial results bitwise identical v0.6.0; serial meat differs ~1e-15 relative new summation algebra. README benchmarks refreshed fixest 0.14.1 scale: 10.7-45.8x cross-sections n = 1M, 1.4-2.9x panel SHAC 1.5M obs (fastconley computes ~T x spatial work construction). brute-force arbitration shows fastconley matches exact great-circle uniform meat ~1e-15 fixest 0.14.1’s “spherical” distance deviates ~2e-2.

title: fastconley 0.6.0
text: meat accumulations use deterministic chunked reduction (fixed-size row/block chunks, partials summed chunk order). ncores = 1 ncores = 16 produce bit-identical matrices — old multicore tolerance caveat gone.

title: fastconley 0.6.0
text: C++ entry points take pre-computed score matrix alias R memory directly (Rcpp input copies, intermediate unsorted score buffer; one gather pass builds sorted layout). vcovSpHAC passes aggregated scores straight ; X/e arguments remain internal wrappers convenience. Measured peak RSS: 4M-row cross-section 2321 -> 1558 MB (-33%); 40k x 40 balanced panel 1028 -> 748 MB (-27%). speed, identical checksums. New csr_weight = c("double", "float"): opt-float storage balanced-path bartlett weights (8 -> 4 bytes per pair, <= ~6e-8 relative error per weight). Default stays exact double.

title: fastconley 0.6.0
text: Haversine gains conservative 3D dot-product pre-screen (exact identity = (1 - dot)/2); exact -test remains arbiter, results bit-identical. CONUS 100k / 500 km bartlett/haversine: 15.1 -> 10.5 s single-threaded (1.4x). Balanced 16-thread uniform meat: 2.30 -> 1.56 s 40k x 40 panel (better task granularity chunked reduction).

title: fastconley 0.6.0
text: unit-major T*k stacked score layout streams balanced CSR instead per period implemented benchmarked. lost period-major layout: spatial sorting makes neighbor gathers sliding window k-wide rows stays L2-resident per period; wider stacking pushes window past L2 thrashes shared L3 high thread counts (2.6 s vs 2.0 s 16 cores). period-major traversal stays, now deterministic float-capable.

title: fastconley 0.5.0
text: spatial meat’s candidate enumeration now defaults 3D cell grid. Points bucketed unit vectors cubic grid whose edge unit-sphere chord equivalent cutoff; every supported distance monotone chord, accepted pairs never one cell apart per axis — pole dateline special cases. row scans cell plus five contiguous row ranges covering 13 forward neighbor cells: ~3–4 candidates per accepted pair, independent geographic extent, versus latitude band scan’s 2*L_lon/(pi*r). strategies call identical per-pair accept test, pair sets weights exactly ; results differ floating-point summation order (observed <= 6e-15 relative across validation matrix; neighbor = "band" remains bitwise identical v0.4.1). band path kept one release removed v0.6.0. Measured single-threaded speedups (FastSpatialMeat, k = 10): global extent, n = 1M, 100 km: 8.6x (uniform/spherical) 25.3x (bartlett/haversine) CONUS, n = 100k, 100 km: 4.5x; 500 km: 2.1-2.3x (config dominated true-pair accumulation, candidate search) balanced CSR build, 200k units x 4 periods, 100 km: 3.6x 16-thread scaling CONUS 100k/500 km improves ~5.3x ~7.9x (less memory-bandwidth pressure candidate streaming)

title: fastconley 0.3.0.9000
text: Adds FastSpatialMeat() internal Rcpp routine. Replaces dense n x n spatial distance matrices vcovSpHAC() screened spatial edge list. Computes meat via cumulative scores: S = e * X, C_i = 0.5 S_i + sum_j w_ij S_j, S'C + C'S. Supports kernel = "bartlett" kernel = "uniform". Supports dist_fn choices: haversine, spherical, chord. upstream flatearth option dropped — formula symmetric (, j) equirectangular approximation longer worth separate code path now spherical+uniform runs 3D dot-product threshold trig. balanced panels, builds one spatial edge list first period reuses periods.

title: fastconley 0.3.0.9000
text: Templated (dist_fn, kernel) dispatch. screen + distance + kernel-weight stack specialised compile time six (distance, kernel) combinations, removing per-pair runtime branches. 3D unit-vector threshold spherical chord. (spherical, uniform) pair inclusion now reduces 3D dot product compared cos(cutoff / R) — trig inner loop. (chord, uniform) uses squared-Euclidean (cutoff / R)². bartlett variants pay acos/sqrt accepted pairs. Row-major score buffer. Scores s_i = e_i · X_i stored row-major single flat std::vector<double> instead recomputed column-major Armadillo memory every pair. Sorted-order layout. coordinate cache scores buffer permuted latitude-sorted order meat workers run, every read hot loop sequential — independent caller laid input. pixel argument score pre-aggregation (R/vcovSpHAC.R). pixel = 0 rows share (lat, lon) within time period collapsed exactly; pixel > 0 rows first snapped uniform pixel-km grid (speed/accuracy trade-). Cross-section vs fixest::vcov_conley (kernel = "uniform", spherical, 500 km cutoff): fastconley now 3-4× faster pixel = 0 27-62× faster pixel = 25 across n ∈ {5k … 100k}, scales better fixest past 4 threads.
